He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Southeastern Fire men's basketball|Southeastern Fire]] and the [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State Eagles]]. ==High school career== Minix played high school basketball for [[Vero Beach High School]] in [[Vero Beach, Florida]]. He experienced a growth spurt before his senior season, where he broke out, averaging 17.4 points and 7.6 rebounds per game. ==College career== He committed to NAIA school [[Southeastern Fire men's basketball|Southeastern]] and was named first-team All-[[Sun Conference]] and conference freshman of the year his first season. In his sophomore year, he suffered an upper-body injury after eight games, sidelining him for the rest of the season.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Glatczak|title=The Comeback Story of Riley Minix and Southeastern U.|url=https://www.collegebasketballtimes.com/post/the-comeback-story-of-riley-minix-and-southeastern-u|website=CollegeBasketballTimes.com|date=March 2022 |publisher=College Basketball Times|access-date=March 7, 2024}} in his next two seasons, Minix was named both a first-team All-American and the Sun Conference Player of the Year.{{cite web|first=Robert|last=Magobet|title=Minix, Southeastern basketball last until NAIA Round of 16; Fire blaze year|url=https://www.theledger.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/03/14/minix-southeastern-play-hard-in-round-of-16/70005425007/|website=TheLedger.com|publisher=[[The Ledger]]|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2024}} Following his four years at Southeastern, Minix chose to take advantage of the extra year given to players due to the interference of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] to transfer up to [[NCAA Division I]], ultimately choosing the Morehead State Eagles.{{cite web|title=All-American Riley Minix Joins Men's Basketball Program for Graduate Season|url=https://msueagles.com/news/2023/4/13/all-american-riley-minix-joins-mens-basketball-program-for-graduate-season.aspx|website=MSUEagles.com|publisher=[[Morehead State Eagles]]|date=April 13, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2024}} In his lone season at Morehead State, Minix finished in the top ten in the [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) in scoring, rebounding, field goal percentage, free throw percentage, blocks, and steals. He also led the conference with 18 [[double-double]]s. At the close of the season, he was named the OVC Player of the Year and a member of the All-OVC first team and All-Newcomer team.{{cite web|title=Morehead State's Minix, Little Rock's Walker and Crocker-Johnson and WIU's Cisse Earn 2023-24 OVC Men's Basketball Top Honors|url=https://ovcsports.com/news/2024/3/4/morehead-states-minix-little-rocks-walker-and-crocker-johnson-and-wius-cisse-earn-2023-24-ovc-mens-basketball-top-honors.aspx|website=OVCSports.com|publisher=[[Ohio Valley Conference]]|date=March 5, 2024|access-date=March 7, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Lyndsey|last=Gough|author-link=Lyndsey Gough|title=Morehead State's Riley Minix named OVC Player of the Year |url=https://www.wkyt.com/2024/03/05/morehead-states-riley-minix-named-ovc-player-year/|website=WKYT.com|publisher=WKYT|date=March 5, 2024|access-date=March 7, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2024–2026)=== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Minix joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]] and on July 20, 2024, he signed with the team.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Spurs Add Minix, Warriors Sign Rowe On Camp Deals|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/spurs-add-minix-warriors-sign-rowe-on-camp-deals.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 21, 2024|access-date=September 1, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Schabert|title=Riley Minix Inks Free Agent Deal With the San Antonio Spurs|url=https://msueagles.com/news/2024/6/28/mens-basketball-riley-minix-inks-free-agent-deal-with-the-san-antonio-spurs.aspx|work=[[Morehead State Eagles]]|date=June 28, 2024|access-date=July 15, 2024}} On October 19, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Spurs.{{cite web|author=sasmcasey|title=Spurs Sign Riley Minix to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-riley-minix-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} During his rookie season, Minix played in only one game for San Antonio, a 100–127 loss against the [[2024–25 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]] on November 26 in which he recorded two rebounds and missed his only shot attempt. Minix would spend the first half of the 2024–25 season with the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. For the Tip - Off Tournament from November 8 to December 22, Minix would instantly be a contributing starter for the club. Averaging 20.5 points, 6.9 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 33 minutes per game. Minix scored in double figures in all 16 games, and scored more than 20 points in 8 of those 16 games, helping them to a 10 - 6 record. For the Austin Spurs, regular season, Minix would only play in the team's first 3 games and averaged 12.7 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 24 minutes per game.{{cite web | title=Riley Minix | url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1642434/boxscores-traditional/?Season=2024-25&SeasonType=Regular%20Season }} After missing the Austin Spurs' next 5 games from January 3 to January 11, on January 15, 2025, it was announced that Minix would miss the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery to repair a torn [[glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his left shoulder.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Spurs' Riley Minix Out For Season Following Shoulder Surgery|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/01/spurs-riley-minix-out-for-season-following-shoulder-surgery.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=January 15, 2025|access-date=January 15, 2025}} On August 6, 2025, Minix re-signed with the Spurs on a two-way contract.{{cite web | title=Spurs Re-Sign Harrison Ingram And Riley Minix To Two-Way Contracts | website=The NBA G League | date=2025-08-06 | url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/spurs-re-sign-harrison-ingram-and-riley-minix-to-two-way-contracts | access-date=2025-12-05}} He made three appearances for San Antonio, averaging 3.0 points, 0.7 rebounds, and 0.3 assists. Minix was waived on December 12, following the signing of [[Kyle Mangas]].{{cite web |title=Riley Minix: Waived by San Antonio |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/riley-minix-waived-by-san-antonio/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=December 13, 2025 |date=December 12, 2025}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers / Charge (2026–present)=== On January 14, 2026, the [[Cleveland Charge]] announced that they had acquired rights to Minix from [[Austin Spurs]] in a three-team trade.{{cite web|title=Charge Acquire Rights to Minix in Trade|url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-acquire-rights-to-minix-in-trade|date=January 14, 2026|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 14, 2026}} On February 13, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] announced that they had signed Minix to a [[two-way contract]]. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- |
